workingTitle: ALMA finds a fully heavy version of methanol around a young star
freshness: Belloche et al. first posted their accepted Astronomy & Astrophysics manuscript on October 5, 2026; ALMA released the result on October 7, 2026. Preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: ALMA COMPASS detected fully deuterated methanol (CD3OD) toward IRAS4A2 in the Perseus molecular cloud, approximately 290 parsecs away.
All four hydrogen atoms in methanol (CH3OH) are replaced by deuterium.
Spectral identification was made by comparison with laboratory line predictions and multi-molecule spectral modeling.
Observed enrichment among methanol isotopic variants is not quantitatively reproduced by current chemical models.
Inferred methanol abundance may be underestimated due to source structure, affecting precise isotope ratios.
caveats: Manuscript accepted for Astronomy & Astrophysics; public preprint first posted October 5, 2026.
The detection is secure but chemical abundance ratios depend on radiative transfer modeling.
The result is not evidence of biology or planets containing the detected molecule.
